problems.title: Invert Binary Tree
problems.statement: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree, and return its root (swap left and right subtrees recursively).
problems.understanding: Inverting a tree means swapping every left child with its corresponding right child at every node in the tree.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Recursive Swap
naive.html: Recursively swap the left and right children.

problems.intuition: Iterative BFS avoids recursion depth issues on deep skewed trees.
problems.approach:
1. If root is None return None.
  2. Push root into BFS queue.
  3. While queue: pop node, swap node.left, node.right = node.right, node.left.
  4. Push left and right children into queue if they exist.

problems.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth (number of nodes along longest path from root to furthest leaf).
problems.understanding: Max depth at root = 1 + max(depth(root.left), depth(root.right)). Base case for empty node is depth 0.

naive.title: Naive Solution — DFS
naive.html: Recursive postorder traversal returning height at each node.

problems.intuition: Level-order traversal (BFS) processes nodes level-by-level using a queue, incrementing depth counter after each level.
problems.approach:
1. If not root return 0.
  2. Initialize queue with root and depth = 0.
  3. For each level (loop size of queue): pop node and push non-null children.
  4. Increment depth after processing level.
problems.takeaway: Both are optimal in time. Choose DFS when recursion is comfortable; BFS naturally gives the number of levels.

problems.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
problems.statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the length of the diameter of the tree (longest path between any two nodes).
problems.understanding: The longest path passing through node u is left_height + right_height. The overall diameter is the max of this value across all nodes.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: For every node, separately calculate the height of its left and right subtree.

problems.intuition: Calculate height and diameter in the same bottom-up DFS traversal.
problems.approach:
1. Initialize diameter = 0.
  2. Define dfs(node): if node is None return 0.
  3. Get left = dfs(node.left) and right = dfs(node.right).
  4. Update diameter = max(diameter, left + right).
  5. Return node height: 1 + max(left, right).
problems.takeaway: Pattern: Postorder DFS + return useful information upward. This pattern is extremely important.

problems.title: Balanced Binary Tree
problems.statement: Given a binary tree, determine if it is height-balanced (left and right subtree heights differ by at most 1 for every node).
problems.understanding: A tree is balanced if abs(height(left) - height(right)) <= 1 for all nodes.
problems.intuition: Return -1 immediately when an unbalanced subtree is found.
problems.approach:
1. Define dfs(node): if node is None return 0.
  2. left = dfs(node.left); if left == -1 return -1.
  3. right = dfs(node.right); if right == -1 return -1.
  4. If abs(left - right) > 1 return -1.
  5. Return 1 + max(left, right).

problems.title: Same Tree
problems.statement: Given roots of two binary trees p and q, check if they are structurally and value identical.
problems.understanding: Both trees must have identical node values and subtree structures at every position.
problems.intuition: Iterative comparison using queue avoids call stack growth.
problems.approach:
1. Push (p, q) into queue.
  2. While queue: pop a, b.
  3. If both None continue. If one None or values differ return False.
  4. Push (a.left, b.left) and (a.right, b.right).

problems.title: Subtree of Another Tree
problems.statement: Given roots of root and subRoot, return true if subRoot is a valid subtree of root.
problems.understanding: For every node in root, check whether subRoot is identical to that subtree.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: For every node in root, check whether subRoot is identical to the subtree.

problems.intuition: Serialize both trees with null markers and run string matching algorithm (KMP) in linear time.
problems.approach:
1. Serialize root and subRoot using preorder traversal into strings with null markers.
  2. Build KMP Partial Match Table (LPS) for pattern string.
  3. Run KMP search to find pattern in text in O(n + m) time.

problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
problems.statement: Given a BST and two nodes p and q, find their Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA).
problems.understanding: In a BST, if both p and q are smaller than root.val, LCA is in left subtree. If both are larger, LCA is in right subtree. Otherwise, root is the split point (LCA).

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: Build paths from root to both nodes.

problems.intuition: Use the BST property directly to traverse without storing path arrays.
problems.approach:
1. While root exists:
  2. If both p.val and q.val < root.val, go left.
  3. If both p.val and q.val > root.val, go right.
  4. Else return root (split point).

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.statement: Given root of a binary tree, return level order traversal of its nodes' values (level by level, left to right).
problems.understanding: Process nodes level by level using BFS or DFS with depth indexing.
problems.intuition: Iterative BFS using a double-ended queue (deque) natural level-by-level processing.
problems.approach:
1. If not root return [].
  2. Push root into deque.
  3. While queue: iterate level size, popleft node, append to level list, push children.
  4. Append level list to result.

problems.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
problems.statement: Given root of a binary tree, return values of nodes visible when looking at tree from right side.
problems.understanding: We want the rightmost node at each depth level of the binary tree.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: DFS right-first and take the first node encountered at every level.

problems.intuition: BFS level-order traversal taking the last element at index size - 1 of each level.
problems.approach:
1. If not root return [].
  2. Queue with root.
  3. For each level: pop nodes, push children left then right.
  4. If `i == size - 1`, append node.val to result.

problems.title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
problems.statement: A node is good if its value is greater than or equal to every value on the path from root.
problems.understanding: Carry state from root → current node to know the maximum value seen so far on the current path.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: Pass complete path array and check node.val == max(path).

problems.intuition: Carry only the single scalar max_so_far value down the branch during DFS.
problems.approach:
1. Define dfs(node, max_so_far).
  2. If node is None return 0.
  3. Check if node.val >= max_so_far.
  4. Update max_so_far = max(max_so_far, node.val).
  5. Recurse left and right subtrees and return total count.
problems.takeaway: Pattern: Carry state from root → current node.

problems.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
problems.statement: Given root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid Binary Search Tree (BST).
problems.understanding: For every node, all left descendants must be strictly smaller, and all right descendants must be strictly larger.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: For every node, calculate max of left subtree and min of right subtree.

problems.intuition: Pass valid lower and upper bounds (low, high) down during DFS traversal.
problems.approach:
1. Define dfs(node, low, high).
  2. If node is None return True.
  3. If not (low < node.val < high) return False.
  4. Recurse dfs(node.left, low, node.val) and dfs(node.right, node.val, high).

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
problems.statement: Given root of BST and integer k, return k-th smallest value (1-indexed) in tree.
problems.understanding: An in-order traversal of a BST visits nodes in strictly ascending sorted order.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: Store the complete inorder traversal in a list and return values[k-1].

problems.intuition: Iterative stack inorder traversal stopping immediately when kth node is reached.
problems.approach:
1. Use explicit stack for inorder traversal.
  2. Push left children until node is None.
  3. Pop node, decrement k. If k == 0 return node.val.
  4. Set node = node.right and continue.

problems.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder & Inorder
problems.statement: Given two integer arrays preorder and inorder, construct and return the binary tree.
problems.understanding: Preorder gives root values sequentially. Inorder splits into left subtree (left of root index) and right subtree (right of root index).
problems.intuition: Use hashmap for O(1) inorder index lookups and preorder index pointer instead of array slicing.
problems.approach:
1. Store positions = {val: i for i, val in enumerate(inorder)}.
  2. Maintain preorder_index = 0.
  3. Define build(left, right): if left > right return None.
  4. Get root_val = preorder[preorder_index], increment pointer, build left and right using mid = positions[root_val].

problems.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
problems.statement: Return maximum path sum of any non-empty path in a binary tree.
problems.understanding: A path can split through current node (left + val + right), but extending to parent can only take ONE branch (val + max(left, right)). Clamp negative branch gains to 0.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: For every node, calculate maximum gain separately.

problems.intuition: Single DFS computing gain to return upward and updating global max path sum.
problems.approach:
1. Initialize answer = -inf.
  2. Define dfs(node): get left = max(0, dfs(node.left)), right = max(0, dfs(node.right)).
  3. Update answer = max(answer, node.val + left + right).
  4. Return single branch gain: node.val + max(left, right).
problems.takeaway: Critical Pattern: Two values: Best path through current node → update answer; Best path going upward → return one branch only.

problems.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
problems.statement: Design an algorithm to serialize a binary tree to a string and deserialize string back to tree.
problems.understanding: Preorder traversal with null marker (#) unambiguously encodes tree structure into flat comma-separated string.

optimal.title: Standard Solution
optimal.html: Preorder traversal with # null markers using string index pointer.
